app_summary: An online shop selling astronomy products, based on the OpenTelemetry Demo. It is built with polyglot microservices (Go, Java, .NET, Python, Node.js, Rust, ...) communicating via gRPC and HTTP behind an Envoy frontend-proxy, with Kafka for asynchronous order processing and Valkey as cart store. Supported Operations: View product catalog, Receive product recommendations and ads, Add item to cart, Checkout with selected items, Currency conversion, Process payment, Generate shipping quotes, Send order confirmation emails

final_report.root_cause: Intermittent cluster DNS (kube-dns / CoreDNS) failures: CoreDNS (10.96.0.10) returned DNS errors ('server misbehaving' / SERVFAIL) while the checkout/payment flow attempted to resolve the hostname 'badAddress'. Those DNS failures caused the payment lookup to fail (gRPC Unavailable) and propagated back through the checkout path to frontend-proxy, causing payment attempts to fail.
final_report.evidence_summary: 1) Observed 20 error traces (sample traceIDs) whose error message is identical: "dns: A record lookup error: lookup badAddress on 10.96.0.10:53: server misbehaving" — the DNS server IP (10.96.0.10) and the exact DNS failure are present in traces. 2) Frontend-proxy traces and logs show it is propagating an upstream gRPC 13/Unavailable error (not generating the DNS error itself). 3) Payment/checkout configuration and Kubernetes service routing are correct: checkout uses PAYMENT_ADDR=payment:8080 and payment Service exposes 8080 with endpoint 10.244.1.21:8080. 4) The payment pod's spec and env do not contain 'badAddress', and container logs do not show a local DNS stack trace for 'badAddress' (they do show a MetadataLookupWarning). 5) kube-dns (ClusterIP 10.96.0.10) has endpoints and the two CoreDNS pods are Running/Ready with 0 restarts, but CoreDNS logs/metrics were not collected in the completed investigations. 6) Together, the trace-level DNS error string plus matching service topology and absence of client misconfiguration point to the DNS server (CoreDNS/kube-dns) returning SERVFAIL/'server misbehaving' as the proximate failing component.
final_report.investigation_summary: Priority-weighted findings: (P1) Payment pod runtime/config was inspected and did not contain an injected 'badAddress' — container environment/volumes and logs (tail) do not corroborate a misconfigured static hostname. A MetadataLookupWarning was observed in payment logs but without hostname details. (P2) Checkout -> Payment DNS/service/port alignment was validated: PAYMENT_ADDR=payment:8080 and payment service endpoints exist. (P3) CoreDNS pod-level health shows two Running pods with 0 restarts (no pod crashes), but CoreDNS logs/metrics were not successfully collected so process-level errors are unobserved. (P4) Payment pod DNS settings are default (ClusterFirst) and kube-dns service endpoints are present. (P5) Frontend-proxy traces and logs demonstrate the proxy is relaying an upstream Unavailable/DNS error from the checkout/payment path, not causing it. (P6) Service port/name checks between frontend-proxy and checkout show correct port mappings. Causal chain: checkout attempted payment -> payment (or client path) triggered DNS lookup for 'badAddress' -> cluster DNS (10.96.0.10) returned 'server misbehaving' -> payment RPC failed with Unavailable -> frontend-proxy propagated error to callers. The strongest direct evidence is the repeated trace error string specifying lookup on 10.96.0.10:53: 'server misbehaving'.
